solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Funny male involved with his pig primarily — a bit of Wodehouse?

indicators.note: funny here means odd or peculiar, telling us these letters go into a peculiar new order
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters of his and pig are used

explanation.surface: A joke about a Wodehouse character and his beloved prize pig, as at Blandings Castle.
explanation.walkthrough: P. G. Wodehouse's first name was Pelham, so the answer is literally one bit of his full name; the question mark flags that playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The author was christened Pelham Grenville, so this is one component of the writer's full name.

clue.text: Board action when BBC boss intercepts English celebrity

indicators.note: to intercept is to cut in on something, so one piece gets inserted into the other

parts.note: a celebrity is a big name
the Director-General heads the BBC, abbreviated DG

explanation.surface: Boardroom drama as the head of the BBC cuts across an English star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board action' suggests a company board, but the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The final phase of a chess game is the play on the board once most pieces are gone.

clue.text: Orthodox Jew can prove who he is, it seems

definitions.meaning: a member of a strictly observant Jewish movement

definitions.text: can prove who he is, it seems
definitions.meaning: someone who can prove his identity carries identification, read as two words

explanation.surface: A religious man able to demonstrate his identity.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as HAS ID: someone who 'has ID' can prove who he is. 'it seems' marks this playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hasid is a follower of Hasidism, a strictly observant movement within Judaism.

clue.text: Silence engulfing a superior part of Oxford? It's a gloomy place

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the first piece surrounds the rest

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'
U is the old British label for upper-class, superior usage
an Oxford is a style of shoe, and its sole is one part of it

explanation.surface: Quietness surrounding an elite corner of Oxford University, described as dismal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the university, but it is a lace-up shoe. U is a crossword convention for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb building housing the dead is fairly called sombre and dark.

clue.text: Fast-moving to catch evil drug supplier

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: pacy means quick or fast-moving
harm is evil or injury

explanation.surface: Something speedy pursuing a wicked drug dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's shop dispenses medicines, a legitimate source of drugs.

clue.text: Fighter to choose love, from what we hear

indicators.note: this signals that the answer is spoken like the phrase in front of it

parts.note: choose is pick, love is adore: spoken together, pick adore

explanation.surface: A combatant opting for romance, apparently according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounted lancer in the bullring fights the bull before the matador.

clue.text: Writer's or writer's writing son's out of order

definitions.meaning: belonging to Kingsley Amis or to his novelist son Martin Amis
wrong, faulty or not as it should be

explanation.surface: A tangle of possessives about a writer and his writing son being in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley Amis was a novelist, and so is his son Martin; either man's property is 'Amis's', which without the apostrophe gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrong or faulty is said to be awry, the sense of being out of order.

clue.text: Rich man goes by man suffering

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so these letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A wealthy man strolls past a man in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a very wealthy person is called by this name for their full purses.

clue.text: Copper came down, having caught pair who did the dirty deed?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: catching something holds it inside, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lit means landed or came down, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A policeman swooped, nabbing a couple suspected of the crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The guilty party is the person responsible for the offence.

clue.text: Sloppy dons in faculty not working properly

indicators.note: sloppy means messy and careless, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Slovenly academics make a university department fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to operate normally is the core sense of this adjective, used of machines and families alike.

clue.text: Letter that's the reverse of funny — and piercing

indicators.note: to pierce is to go into, so one piece is inserted in the other
reverse here means turned backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: droll means amusing or funny

explanation.surface: A letter that is the opposite of humorous, and cutting with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests an alphabet character or a missive; here it is someone who lets property.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rents out property to tenants is the person who lets it.

clue.text: Dorothy? A philosopher among saints

indicators.note: being among things means sitting between them, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A woman named Dorothy, a thinker among the holy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L. Sayers was the crime novelist who created Lord Peter Wimsey; the question mark shows Dorothy is one example.

clue.text: One will have let the French find out

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)
to see is to find out, as in 'I'll see if he's in'

explanation.surface: Someone permitting the French to discover something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let' reads as allow, but here it means rented: a tenant has a property let to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant who holds a lease is the party to whom a property has been rented.

clue.text: Sober quality of Thames-side town restricting daughter and son

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the town holds the next piece within it

parts.note: Staines is a town on the River Thames west of London

explanation.surface: The sensible character of a riverside town that keeps its children in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Staines (now Staines-upon-Thames) is a commuter town on the Thames in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sedate and serious, never frivolous, is the trait of sober people.

clue.text: Causes to divert sports official — right little performances!

parts.note: ref is short for referee
acts are short turns in a variety show

explanation.surface: A referee makes a fuss about players' theatrical play-acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divert' suggests entertaining, but it is bending a ray of light.
explanation.definitionFit: When light passes into glass or water its path is bent, or turned aside, by the medium.

clue.text: Joking and argumentative about source of energy

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: factious means given to faction and dispute

indicators.note: the source is where something starts, so only the first letter of energy is used

explanation.surface: Bantering yet quarrelsome over where power comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating serious matters flippantly, with ill-timed humour, is this adjective's sense.

clue.text: One to remove defences or ridicule protection, we hear

indicators.note: this signals that the answer sounds like the words before it

parts.note: diss is slang for ridicule and armour is protection; spoken together, diss armour

explanation.surface: Someone who takes away weapons, or mocks body armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes away weapons and defences, rendering others harmless, fits this agent noun.

clue.text: Nourishment provided by catering establishment

indicators.note: the letters are supplied from inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Food supplied by a restaurant or canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the technical term for material taken into the body as food.

clue.text: Maybe convert ground and it can hold game

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A rugby convert scored at a recreation ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convert' suggests a rugby kick, fitting 'ground' and 'game', but it is a new adherent; 'Maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone newly enlisted to a cause or group, as a convert is to a faith, is a new member.

clue.text: Cordial Conservative given inadequate help

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to assist is to help

explanation.surface: A friendly Tory receives insufficient support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like an adjective, friendly, but is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Crème de cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur, a sweet drink of the kind called a cordial.

clue.text: Favoured an exceptionally small city in a silly way

parts.note: in means in favour, as in 'in with the boss'
Ely in Cambridgeshire is one of England's smallest cities

explanation.surface: Someone preferred a tiny city, foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, famous for its small size.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something pointlessly and foolishly, without sense, is the adverb's meaning.

clue.text: African city offers atmosphere in which old tribe can settle

indicators.note: in which points to the first piece as the container for what follows
settling somewhere means living within it, so the tribe goes inside

parts.note: air is atmosphere
Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: A North African city with an ambience where an ancient people might put down roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a Moroccan port and resort on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Soldier abandoning battalion finally to become gardener?

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, not an officer

indicators.note: finally picks out only the final letter of battalion

explanation.surface: A soldier leaves the army at last and takes up gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: One who uses a rake on lawns and beds is a garden worker, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Big mammal placed on a vast continent reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the answer sounds like the words before it

parts.note: placed is set and on the vast continent of Asia is Asian; spoken together, set Asian

explanation.surface: A large animal located in Asia, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales and dolphins form this order of marine mammals, including the largest animal ever.

clue.text: Explorer to get cold, say

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to aver is to state or say

explanation.surface: An adventurer gets chilly, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A potholer explores underground passages, so is one kind of explorer.

clue.text: Meat dish that could do for a US VIP eater, OK?

indicators.note: could do for suggests the letters might be reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A dish suited to an American bigwig who likes his food: is that all right?
explanation.definitionFit: This French classic is a beef cut coated in crushed peppercorns.

clue.text: Language of saint carrying a new and terrible risk

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the rest goes inside
terrible means awful or wrecked, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A holy man's speech bearing a fresh and dreadful danger.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient classical tongue of India, used in Hindu scripture.

clue.text: Waifs bringing glimmers of sunshine to street

parts.note: rays are beams of light from the sun

explanation.surface: Homeless children brightening a road with cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost or homeless creatures, especially pets or children, are wanderers without a home.
